title: Density effects in precision laser spectroscopy of exotic helium atoms
authors: Hubert J. Jóźwiak, Dimitar Bakalov, Michał Przybytek, Michail Stoilov, Piotr Wcisło
abstract: Exotic helium atoms act as unique atomic traps for heavy, negatively charged particles, protecting them from nuclear annihilation and nuclear capture on timescales long enough to enable high-precision laser spectroscopy. Such measurements serve as stringent tests of three-body quantum electrodynamics and offer a direct route to determining fundamental particle masses. Motivated by upcoming spectroscopic efforts targeting pionic ($π^{-\,4}\mathrm{He}^+$) and kaonic ($K^{-\,4}\mathrm{He}^+$) helium, we present a rigorous theoretical evaluation of the collisional and density effects governing these systems. Using an ab initio potential energy surface and coupled-channel quantum scattering calculations, we study the collisional stability of the candidate metastable states against inelastic quenching in a cryogenic helium buffer gas. Furthermore, we provide theoretical reference values for the pressure broadening and pressure shift coefficients of the targeted transitions. These results establish an essential benchmark for future experiments, paving the way for refined determinations of the pion and kaon masses.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical evaluation of density and collisional effects governing high-precision laser spectroscopy on exotic helium atoms, such as pionic and kaonic helium. Using advanced coupled-channel quantum scattering calculations, the authors derive essential benchmark values for pressure broadening and shifts. These results are crucial for future experiments aiming to test fundamental constants and determine the masses of particles like the pion and kaon.
main_problem: To provide a rigorous theoretical benchmark for high-precision laser spectroscopy on exotic helium atoms ($	ext{X}^-	ext{He}^+$) by calculating collisional and density effects.
main_result: The authors provide theoretical reference values for the pressure broadening and shift coefficients for targeted transitions in pionic and kaonic helium, essential for future mass determinations.
method: The study employs coupled-channel quantum scattering calculations using an ab initio potential energy surface (PES) derived from super-molecular approaches.
model_or_system: The system involves exotic helium atoms ($	ext{X}^-	ext{He}^+$ where $	ext{X}^-$ is a heavy negative particle like $\pi^-$ or $K^-$) interacting with a cryogenic helium buffer gas. The physics tests three-body quantum electrodynamics.
key_observables: Transition frequencies, pressure broadening coefficients ($\gamma_0$), and pressure shift coefficients ($\delta_0$).
important_parameters: The required accuracy for spectroscopy is extremely high (e.g., $	ext{P} \propto 100 	ext{ GHz}$ needed for $\pi^-	ext{He}^+$). Metastable states must survive Auger decay.
main_assumptions: Calculations are performed within the Born–Oppenheimer approximation, and line-shape calculations often utilize a single-state basis due to convergence tests showing negligible impact from nearest neighbors on broadening/shift parameters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical state space of exotic helium atoms (Fig. 1) and show calculated pressure broadening ($	ext{Re}(\sigma_c)$) and shift ($	ext{Im}(\sigma_c)$) cross-sections for specific transitions in pionic and kaonic helium.
paper_structure: The paper systematically addresses the need for theoretical benchmarks, first evaluating collisional stability against quenching, and then calculating the necessary line-shape parameters (broadening/shift coefficients) using advanced quantum scattering methods.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of precision spectroscopy by providing the necessary theoretical corrections for complex many-body interactions in exotic atomic systems. It directly informs experimental feasibility in AMO physics.

FIG. 3: Leading inelastic quenching cross sections, σ(v,j)→(v+1,j−1), originating from the three collisionally robust metastable states in (a) pionic helium and (b) kaonic helium. The color scheme matches the effective isotropic expansion coefficients of the PES presented in Fig. 2, where the initial metastable state for each transition corresponds to the solid line of the identical color. For the pionic n = 18 manifold (orange), we present cross-sections for both the metastable (v = 1, j = 16) state (solid line) and the experimentally relevant (v = 0, j = 17) state (dashed line), whose Auger lifetime is currently unavailable in the literature.
